headline: the renderer's `effective_speed` replica omits the engine's `weather_is_active` guard, so AIR LOCK and CLOUD NINE do not suppress weather for it. That flips the computed move order, and because `segment()` tries only the order it computes, the ENTIRE branch is voided as `segmentation_failed`.
status: CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIX VERIFIED CORRECT. Not shippable alone -- it exposes an interaction worth 6 rows. Both must land together.
this_causes_the_last_uncaused_rows: 19000093/51 AND 19000093/53. Both close under the fix. Clause 1's remaining gap is closed by this.

the_measurement_that_found_it.probe: printed the renderer's effective_speed for both sides plus every input field, at the segmentation_failed site.
the_measurement_that_found_it.output: eff1=261 eff2=348 raw1=174 raw2=174 weather=RAIN st1=NONE st2=NONE boost1=1 boost2=0 ab1=AIRLOCK ab2=SWIFTSWIM
the_measurement_that_found_it.the_read: Rayquaza (SideOne) has AIR LOCK; Seaking (SideTwo) has SWIFT SWIM; it is RAINING. The replica doubled Seaking to 348 against Rayquaza's 261 and declared SideTwo first. The engine suppressed the rain and moved SideOne first -- which the pair-generated list confirms, since it BEGINS with `Damage SideTwo`, i.e. SideTwo receiving.
the_measurement_that_found_it.the_source_difference: engine `get_effective_speed` wraps its weather match in `if state.weather_is_active(&state.weather.weather_type)`. The renderer's replica has NO guard. Everything else about the two functions is identical -- I diffed the modifier lists in reports/c107 and they match, which is why the formula was ruled out and the inputs were the remaining place to look.
the_measurement_that_found_it.blast_radius_beyond_order: any renderer consumer of effective_speed inherits it. Air Lock is a Rayquaza ability and Rayquaza is common in this pool.

the_fix.form: wrap the weather match in `state.weather_is_active(...)`, mirroring the engine.
the_fix.measured: transition:matched 15208 -> 15205, transition:diverged 15 -> 19, strict:lossy_render 11 -> 0, skip:strict_all_branches_lossy 1 -> 0. Both sides reconcile to 15224, 0 engine errors, 94 lib tests pass.
the_fix.closed: 19000093/51 and 19000093/53 -- BOTH segmentation rows, which is the whole remaining clause-1 gap.
the_fix.lossy_render_to_zero: the counter that actually tracks this defect went to ZERO. Segmentation now succeeds on every branch in the corpus.

the_interaction_that_blocks_shipping.what_happens: the same six rows the faint-without-damage fix closed re-open: 19000024/61, 19000077/47, 19000089/53, 19000098/79, 19000152/53, 19000199/61. Net +4.
the_interaction_that_blocks_shipping.why_it_is_an_INTERACTION_and_not_a_regre: those six boundaries were previously VOIDED by the very segmentation failure this fix repairs -- their branches were lossy and excluded from comparison. Now they render, so they are compared for the first time, and they diverge. The fix did not break them; it made them visible.
the_interaction_that_blocks_shipping.the_likely_mechanism_NOT_YET_CONFIRMED: the faint synthesis added to the parser in the C96 fix runs on ANY protocol passed to `damage_components`, including the ENGINE's newly-rendered one. If the engine's rendered protocol carries both a `-damage ... 0 fnt` for its Damage instruction and a bare `|faint|`, the synthesis may add a phantom component on the engine side. I have NOT verified this and am not claiming it -- it is the first thing to check.
the_interaction_that_blocks_shipping.the_decisive_check: replay one of the six with the Air Lock fix applied and compare the engine branch's component list against its rendered protocol. One run.
the_interaction_that_blocks_shipping.why_this_is_good_news_not_bad: it means the six rows were never really closed -- they were closed against a voided engine branch. The C96 fix's measured -6 was partly an artifact of comparing against nothing. That is exactly the class of defect PR #1038 was written about, and it would have stayed hidden without this fix.

disposition.sequencing: land with the interaction resolved, and re-measure the combined effect. Do NOT ship the Air Lock guard alone at +4, and do NOT drop it -- it is correct and it is the only thing that closes the two segmentation rows.
disposition.gate: a pin on effective_speed under AIR LOCK plus RAIN plus SWIFT SWIM that fails when the guard is reverted, and a sweep reporting matched, skip and lossy together.
